captions.text: Recap of chapters 21 and 22: chunks that keep their title found facts basic RAG missed.
KeywordIndex finds exact words, such as codes, that vectors miss.
HybridIndex joins the two searches into one ranking.
And you learned not to rank scores that sit close together.
Today's black box: an agent that does its own searching.
Let's open it. But first, a question one search can't answer.
How much notice must a shift lead give? You need their band, then that band's rule.
Those are two files. Predict: will one search find both?
It found the rule, and not the band. So the model made one up: Band E, 8 weeks.
A shift lead is Band C, so it's 4 weeks. Wrong in 5 runs of 5.
Why not fetch more hits? Predict: where does pay-bands.md rank?
Rank 134 of 934. The question is about resigning, not roles.
No k passes. And 2,050 tokens at k=134 is chapter 20's silent cut.
So let the agent do the looking. search_tool turns any index into a tool.
The model reads these words, so they're the tool's instructions.
It runs the search you already have, and returns the same excerpts as Rag.
The system prompt even names this case: search for a band.
Nothing here is new. It's chapter 12's loop, and the tool is a search.
The model writes the query, and decides whether to go round again.
The same question, printing every query. Predict: how many searches?
One. It wrote a tidy query, and never looked up the band.
So it hedged across the bands. 2 model calls: one to search, one to answer.
Now measure. 42 questions, three runs each, and each agent twice.
Keep records what each run searched for, which a Report doesn't. Predict the winner.
One-shot setups: 97 to 105. These checks accept "tie" and "ten", corrected.
Agents: 112 to 119. Every agent row wins, by at least 7. The clearest gain in Part 4.
Hop looks solved, at 12 to 15 of 18. You've just seen one search. Be suspicious.
It isn't free. About 2 model calls per question, against 1.
And about 900 tokens, against 500. We make no claim about speed: the machine was shared.
agent60 searched more than once in only 9 runs of 252. On hop, just 3 of 36.
They retry with new words. None looks up a second fact from the first result.
So is it the loop, or the query? Give plain Rag the agent's first query.
101, about 4 above titles60 with no loop. A short query beats a chatty question.
But hop is 3, against the agent's 12. So read those hop passes.
An answer listing every band contains "4 weeks", so it passed. A stricter check says no.
Loose 27, strict 14. And 16:00 had passed for 6:00, a bug in our check.
Both repair questions pass, but each branch file holds the number. No hop needed.
The four real hops: no run saw both files. 0 of 48, across both agents.
Rescore everything. Agents 107 to 114, one-shot 96 to 102. The lead holds.
But hop is 7 or 8 of 18. The agent made multi-hop look solved, and it wasn't.
Each search found the right rule. Then the model wrote "I assume" or "likely" and guessed.
Questions with no answer: 6 failures in 72 runs. Four are declines in other words.
One ran out of steps. And one, after 6 searches, said dogs aren't allowed.
The handbook doesn't say that. It's rare, 1 in 72, but it reads like a policy.
Can we fix it? First, tell it harder. Predict: how many of 30 runs see both files?
One. The prompt names this exact case, and the model still doesn't do it.
Second, stop and ask the model what's missing, in a separate call.
Worse. It nearly always replies NONE. It can't see what isn't there.

Both files in 11 of 30, and a pass now comes from having the facts.
On everything: 105 and 106. Above one search, and below the agents.
But on the real hops, both files came back in 12 of 24 runs. For agents, 0 of 48.
It's a direction, not a result. We wrote that prompt after reading these failures.
Be fair: chapter 20's whole files, with a big window, scored 103. One call.
And the pasted handbook scored hop 16 of 18, with chapter 20's looser checks.
So agents won among these setups. That isn't everything you could build.

You've finished when you see 5 passed.

Better chunks and search fixed real failures, and the agent gave the biggest gain.
